Population increased in Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole

The estimated population of Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole in 2024 was 408,967 usual residents, a rise of 0.6% since 2023.

This meant that Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole's rate of population change placed it about average among local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole increased by 2.2%.

Over this slightly longer period, Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole was also among the areas that had a broadly average population increase, of local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole

The average (median) age rose to 42.6 years between 2023 and 2024.

sections.content:
Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole is an area that is classed as urban in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole's population of 408,967 usual residents was made up of:

  • 65,972 people aged 0 to 15 years, (16.1%)
  • 254,144 people aged 16 to 64 years, (62.1%)
  • 88,851 people aged 65 years and over, (21.7%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole has a slightly higher proportion of people aged 65 years and over (21.7% compared with 18.9% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net international migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More deaths than births led to a fall in the population of 1,285 people (-0.3%). In total, there were 3,153 births and 4,438 deaths in Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) led to a fall in the population of 794 (-0.2%). There were 23,834 people entering the area and 24,628 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole's population of 4,424 (1.1%) as a result of 7,568 people entering the area and 3,144 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole in mid-2023 is 406,626.

Within this, international migration was revised upwards by 2,647 people and internal migration estimates were revised downwards by 71 people.

Overall, there was an revision upwards of 2,576 people.
